title: [Bug]: Speculative decoding (mtp and dflash) silently disables prefix-cache hits for hybrid GDN models on nightly; worked on v0.24.0
body:
(analysis by Fable 5)
### Your current environment

- DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121`/`sm_121a`, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory), Docker `--network host --gpus all --ipc host`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` → reports `v0.28.1rc1.dev43+g6f7df92a8`
- Comparison baseline on the same host: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0`
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (hybrid GDN: 48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers, built-in MTP head). Also reproduced with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (rev `dedf8df`).
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 65536`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30`, env `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the current nightly, enabling **any** speculative decoding method (built-in `mtp` or `dflash`) on a hybrid GDN model silently drops `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` to **0** — align-mode prefix caching engages at startup (log: `Mamba cache mode is set to 'align' for Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) but never hits, and repeated long prompts pay full re-prefill. The identical command minus `--speculative-config` hits normally. No crash, no warning — the caching is just inert, so this is easy to miss in production.

A/B on the same host, same model, same 18,219-token prompt sent twice (`max_tokens=10`):

| nightly config | TTFT req1 → req2 | `prefix_cache_hits_total` delta |
|---|---|---|
| APC only (no spec) | 9.46 s → **0.64 s** | **17,248** |
| APC + `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` | 23.6 s → 13.9 s* | **0** |
| APC + `{"method":"dflash", ..., "num_speculative_tokens":7}` | 12.9 s → 12.5 s | **0** |

\* the MTP row also shows a large decode regression on this platform (10.5 tok/s vs 19.7 on v0.24.0 with the same flags — possibly a separate sm_121 issue; noting it for context, not the subject of this report).

**On `v0.24.0`, MTP + align-mode APC coexist correctly** on the same host/model: repeated 9,901-token prompt → 8,000 tokens hit, TTFT 7.27 s → 1.33 s, with `mtp` k=3 active. So spec+APC coexistence for hybrids existed and regressed somewhere between v0.24.0 and the current nightly.

Repro (nightly):

```bash
docker run --rm --init --network host --gpus all --ipc host \
  -v /opt/models:/models -e CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a \
  vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /models/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4 \
  --served-model-name bench --port 10099 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# send any >3,300-token prompt twice; watch vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total stay 0
# drop --speculative-config and the second send hits ~all full blocks
```

Possibly related but distinct: #53670 (hits occur but recompute per hit), #41884 (DFlash+APC IndexError crash — we see silent zero-hit, not a crash), #26201 (tracking).

Is the suppression intentional (spec-decode + hybrid APC support not yet wired on the new path), or a regression? If intentional, a startup warning like the align-mode one would save users from silently losing their cache. Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware.
